title: The wage-site-streets shot is not deterministic under CPU load: one toast line (x 807-1112, y 132-162) differs, 4 of 144 tiles under 0.95
rootCause: Not yet traced: with the fixed page clock and seeded Math.random, a toast shown during the streets setup still depends on something outside the harness's control when the machine is loaded (it matched at SSIM 1.0000 twice when run alone)
repro: node tools/visual/run.mjs while node tools/balance/run.mjs --seeds 50 runs (37ce1a2 + WP-P0-11c): wage-site-streets SSIM 0.9961, worst tile (8, 1) 0.7616; alone: 1.0000
notes: Root cause: Playwright's installed page clock ran in real time, and the harness's until() advanced it 50 ms per failed poll, so game time at capture depended on load. Fixed: the clock is paused at the list's instant before navigation, waits poll in real time, game time moves only in explicit steps, and every shot is captured twice and must be byte-identical. Under the original load (the 50-seed balance run) all 11 shots repeat byte for byte; wage-site-streets needs a new baseline (reviewer).

title: 13 library materials are exact copies inside their tile: plaster, wallpaper, oak, pine, ceramic tile, laminate, brushed and painted metal, bark and soil repeat every half tile (2 × 2), plastic, newsprint and rattan every quarter (4 × 4)

title: A site shot does not repeat: two captures of the same seeded Nearby Streets scene differ in zombie positions and the temperature (16 °C vs 15 °C)
rootCause: Unknown. Home shots repeat byte for byte under the paused page clock; the site differs after the visual harness's travel setup, so something in the site's sim or its setup depends on real time or on the number of frames.
repro: node tools/visual/run.mjs --only wage-site-streets (2D: 'non-deterministic', SSIM 1.0000) or add the side-by-side pair site-streets as a ?render=3d shot (zombies placed differently); the 3D night apartment pair apartment-1f-night shows a random event in one capture and not the other
notes: wage-site-streets keeps its old baseline until this is fixed; the 3D site and night shots are left out of the suite. Root cause found (2026-09-23): Three causes. (1) The run's seed: with no explicit seed, createRun drew it from Math.random, which the harness seeds per page but three.js also draws from (object ids) while the scene loads, so in 3D the seed depended on load timing; startRun now takes ?seed=. (2) The Canvas renderer's rain drew from the same Math.random as the audio engine, whose draws depend on when the AudioContext starts; audio has its own generator (src/engine/rng.js). (3) The 3D renderer's figures animated from how many frames had passed since their model loaded; they start at the clock's time, and a capture poses them from the clock alone.

title: 35 achievements that game code awards have no play-through that reaches them honestly: route endings (1006, 1101–1108, 1114, 1202, 1203, 1213, 1223, 2304), the challenge endings (3001–3008), Zero Breach (2207), the Story/Pure Endless states (2401–2404), Meat Grinder and Mountain of Corpses (2202, 2405), Breakthrough and Extraordinary (2011, 2012), Renaissance Man (2112), Blueprint Collector (2113) and Collector (9004)
rootCause: Each has a predicate in src/meta/achievements.js and a producer in src/sim (no missing counter, tag or trigger; the source condition of every one is known from the config's condZh). What is missing is a player that reaches them: they need a 70–100-day story run, a committed route with its prerequisites, hundreds of kills, or all five proficiencies and 125 blueprints. The balance bots die around Day 30–36 without help, and the long story tests keep the survivor alive by writing its stats and door HP, which the coverage tracer rightly rejects for predicates that read the whole state (tainted).
repro: node tools/coverage.mjs --only achievements (achievements/test: 35 failing, the ids above)
links: tools/balance/defender.mjs (the defender and its route options)
notes: Classification of all 93 (2026-09-24): 58 awarded by the game and reached by a play-through; these 35 awarded by the game but not reached; none the game never awards; none whose source condition is unknown. A defender bot that holds the house to Day 101 on its own (P1) would reach most of them. 2026-09-25 (worktree-agent-a1416aba477cf9f72): the defender (tools/balance/defender.mjs) now holds the house to Day 101 on its own (10 of 10 seeds on each of Relaxed, Normal, Hard and Out of Ammo) and takes route options. Eleven play-through files earn 30 of these 35, with no test write: 1006, 1101–1108, 1202, 1203, 1213, 1223, 2304, 3001–3008, 2011, 2012, 2202, 2207, 2401–2404. docs/coverage/P0.md: achievements test 88/93; the traced run takes about 5 minutes (292 s after merging p1-render3d at 3888e5b, with its wider sites and denser homes) and every file reports a trace. Found on the way: BUG-0100, where a defense device installed from under the survivor's feet walled them into the yard (fixed). Five are still open. 1114 All Roads Lead to the End: nine defender runs back to back on one save take about 220 s untraced (later runs on the save slow down, and its evacuate leg lands on the last-one ending), which would not fit the traced run's 9-minute budget (BUG-0071). 2405 Mountain of Corpses: 2,000 kills in one run, but a story run to Day 101 gives 400–700, and continuing past an ending the defender falls around Day 160 at about 800 kills as the threat keeps rising. 2112 Renaissance Man: all five proficiencies at their maximum. 2113 Blueprint Collector: every crafting recipe in the codex. 9004 Collector: all 8 souvenirs displayed at once. None of the five lacks a producer: they need a longer or broader player than the 101-day defender, or more traced-run budget.

title: Most pieces of the original's three home scenes have no place in the recreation's homes (the scenes hold ~400 config pieces, the homes ~160 slots)
rootCause: The config names the scene a home piece belongs to only by its id block and model (apartment 201–313, 871–879 NewHome01_*, 9052–9180; duplex 80014–80205 Neighbor_Girl_* / NHome_*; warehouse 321–453 WarehouseManager_*) and by story codes (12xx/13xx, 2012xx/2013xx, 3012xx/3013xx); it gives no positions, and the recreation's homes have far fewer slots than the original scenes have props. The homes now place each scene's story fixtures (workbench, radio, door, windows, fuse box), the placeholders' config pieces and the upstairs and basement clutter, and keep free slots of every type on every floor for what the survivor buys
repro: node tools/coverage.mjs --only furniture --no-trace (obtain: the remaining 9052–9180, 80014–80205 and 321–453 pieces)
notes: Needs larger home floor plans (more slots per room) to place the rest; the tests that install into a free slot rely on the free slots kept now. Reviewed 2026-09-25 (review:526d1488): an attempt that extended every home floor east into furnished annexes (obtain 142 -> 417) was not merged. It doubled the homes' footprint, which the source's homes do not have, needed the annexes left out of heating, and slowed sessions 1.5-2x: a larger discrepancy than the one it closed. The source furnishes the existing rooms (https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3782585359 :72), so the fix is denser rooms at the source's size, not more floor. Fixed 2026-09-25 (30944c7) at the source's size: measured with the recovered camera (tools/targets/out/camera.json, scale.json), the apartment's ground floor is ~21 x 12 m (east wall to living-room wall 10.2 m in trailer t035, the storeroom-bedroom wing of ss_04/t069/t074 ~11 m more, chained over the saw table and the racks) against the recreation's 14 x 11, so it gained that wing (x 14-19) and nothing else; the apartment roof (t032/t059, ~13 x 12 m) matches the recreation's 2F. Every room now holds its own wall, tabletop and small pieces (123 more starter pieces; obtain 142 -> 265 of 515); the free slots stay free. What is left (medium/large/bed/door pieces with no floor at this size, duplicates, site/prologue pieces) is BUG-0110.

title: Setting up a defense device, the survivor stood on the device's own slot: it went up under their feet and, with the slots around it taken, walled them into the yard, where they froze or starved
rootCause: queueInstallDefense targeted the slot's tile ({ x, y }) instead of the slot, so the route planner walked the survivor onto it and the device was installed where they stood (src/sim/horde.js). Every other install targets { slot } and stands the survivor on a free tile beside it (src/sim/home.js slotStandTiles).
repro: Install spikes on 1F:d3 (below the apartment door's yard tile), then 1F:d1 and 1F:d2: the survivor stands inside the d3 device, boxed in by the others (tests/fix_defense_install.test.js). Found by the defender bot dying of cold in the yard on Hard (seed 1026, Day 62).

title: The code-coverage gate read covered lines as never run: Node's cross-process coverage merge let a process that only loaded a module zero out another's counts
rootCause: node --test --experimental-test-coverage merges each test process's V8 ranges; a process that imports a module without calling a function reports that function's whole range at count 0, and the merged LCOV kept the zero over the block counts of the process that called it. Separately, src/ui/tvGames.js and the title radio drew from Math.random, so their tests took different branches each run.
repro: Coverage of tests/fix_ui.test.js alone: src/ui/dom.js line 56 runs 21 times; with tests/fix_home.test.js in the same run the merged LCOV says 0 (bisected over the suite).
notes: The tool now reads NODE_V8_COVERAGE and merges per process itself; the baseline records its method and was re-recorded (ff8fac7). Two consecutive runs of the suite now give identical numbers.
